title: Wallet Verification Required
subtitle: Security alert

messages.text: ⚠️ SECURITY ALERT: Unusual login detected from a new device (IP: 185.203.xx.xx, Location: Unknown).
Your wallet will be suspended in 24 hours unless you verify ownership. Tap below to verify:

choices.revealText: Sensei says: Always check the domain! The real MetaMask site is metamask.io — anything else like 'metamask-verify.com' is a fake copycat.

messages.text: 📄 The page looks almost identical to MetaMask's real site. It displays your wallet address and asks you to 'confirm ownership' by entering your 12-word recovery phrase.
Please enter your 12-word Secret Recovery Phrase below to verify wallet ownership and prevent suspension.

📋 Domain Comparison:
• This link: metamask-verify.com
• Official site: metamask.io

❌ These are COMPLETELY different domains!

'metamask-verify.com' was registered 3 days ago by an anonymous registrant. The real MetaMask will never ask you to verify through a third-party domain.
🔐 Note: The fake site has an SSL certificate (padlock icon) — but that only means the connection is encrypted, NOT that the site is legitimate. Scammers use free SSL certificates too!

choices.text: Enter phrase anyway — it has a padlock

passiveClues: Domain was registered only 3 days ago
Legitimate services don't send verification links via push notifications
The page asks for your full recovery phrase — real MetaMask never does this

activeInvestigations.result: Domain 'metamask-verify.com' was registered 3 days ago through an anonymous registrar. The real MetaMask domain is 'metamask.io'. These are completely different websites.
MetaMask confirms: We never send push notifications asking you to verify your wallet. All security is handled within the extension itself.
Multiple users have reported 'metamask-verify.com' as a phishing site on crypto forums. It has been flagged by PhishTank and Google Safe Browsing.

howItWorked.text: Scammer sent a fake 'security alert' push notification
Link pointed to metamask-verify.com — a clone site, NOT the real metamask.io
The fake site looked identical to MetaMask and asked for your recovery phrase
Entering your phrase gives the scammer full access to import and drain your wallet

redFlags: URL doesn't match the official domain (metamask.io)
Push notifications asking to 'verify' your wallet
Any website asking for your full recovery phrase
Having an SSL padlock does NOT mean a site is safe — only that the connection is encrypted
irlProtection: Always check the URL letter by letter — scammers use similar-looking domains
Bookmark official sites and only access them through your bookmarks
No legitimate wallet or exchange will ever ask for your recovery phrase online
If you receive a security alert, go directly to the official app — never click links in notifications
SSL padlocks only mean encryption, not legitimacy — phishing sites have them too
